classification.difficultyReason: Calculate two side gradients and use their product to prove that the triangle has a right angle.

content.prompt: Show that the points $(1,4)$, $(-4,-1)$ and $(2,3)$ are the vertices of a right-angled triangle.

answer.short:
$m_{AB}=1$ and $m_{AC}=-1$, so $AB\perp AC$. The right angle is at $(1,4)$.

The product of the two gradients is $-1$.
answer.worked:
Let $A=(1,4)$, $B=(-4,-1)$ and $C=(2,3)$.

$$\begin{align*}m_{AB}&=\frac{-1-4}{-4-1}\\m_{AB}&=\frac{-5}{-5}\\m_{AB}&=1\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}m_{AC}&=\frac{3-4}{2-1}\\m_{AC}&=-1\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}m_{AB}m_{AC}&=1\times(-1)\\m_{AB}m_{AC}&=-1\end{align*}$$

Therefore $AB\perp AC$, so $\angle BAC=90^\circ$. The points are the vertices of a right-angled triangle.
